content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text calls the Isaiah 7:14 issue UNDERDETERMINED because the chapter bounds and Matthew 1:23 application both stand and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways, so it treats a two-sense verse as open.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand: I weighed whether this forbids UNDERDETERMINED for a two-sense verse, or instead permits UNDERDETERMINED after both senses are acknowledged.","why":"The judge's UNDERDETERMINED rests on the word-count cutting both ways while both the chapter bounds and Matthew application stand, which is exactly treating a two-sense verse as open rather than letting both senses stand."}
